scope: SF10 32 native terminals plus one sensitive StockLevel query under the 4-core CPU bottleneck profile
direction_semantics: T[param][resource] is the signed physical-resource effect of increasing one PostgreSQL planner cost parameter while other parameters are fixed

derivation_contract.semantic_chain: parameter increase -> planner path preference -> expected plan-node mix -> expected CPU/memory/read+write IO direction
derivation_contract.qps_policy: QPS is excluded from T and from the small-loop SGD score; measured db_qps is used only by the real-replay outer acceptance gate
derivation_contract.real_evidence_count_semantics: evidence_count counts independently attributable real replays only; semantic reasoning does not increment it
derivation_contract.confidence_semantics: low prior weight used by the SGD direction calculation; it is not a posterior probability
derivation_contract.multi_parameter_replay_policy: a joint vector replay may support that exact vector but cannot be split into independent per-parameter causal signs

seq_page_cost.plan_effect: higher cost discourages sequential scans and can favor index/bitmap access
seq_page_cost.resource_effect: usually fewer heap pages and filtered tuples, but index traversal makes CPU sign weak
seq_page_cost.historical_relation: CPU sign agrees with the old joint vector; IO decrease agrees; individual attribution is absent

random_page_cost.plan_effect: higher cost discourages index and bitmap paths and can favor sequential scans
random_page_cost.resource_effect: more scanned pages and tuples generally raise CPU and total read+write IO
random_page_cost.historical_relation: resource signs agree with the old table, but the old source was one multi-parameter vector

cpu_tuple_cost.plan_effect: higher cost penalizes plans that process many tuples and favors earlier row reduction
cpu_tuple_cost.resource_effect: fewer processed tuples tends to reduce CPU, memory working set and IO
cpu_tuple_cost.historical_relation: resource signs agree with the old table; individual attribution is absent

cpu_index_tuple_cost.plan_effect: higher cost discourages index paths and can switch to broader heap/sequence access
cpu_index_tuple_cost.resource_effect: broader scans generally raise CPU, working set and IO
cpu_index_tuple_cost.historical_relation: memory and IO signs conflict with or are unsupported by the old table, so confidence is lowest

cpu_operator_cost.plan_effect: higher cost penalizes expression, predicate, sort and join work and favors plans applying work to fewer rows
cpu_operator_cost.resource_effect: expected CPU and IO decrease is weak because alternative plan shapes can trade CPU for IO
cpu_operator_cost.historical_relation: CPU sign agrees with the old joint vector; independent attribution is absent

parallel_setup_cost.plan_effect: higher cost discourages Gather/Gather Merge and parallel-aware children
parallel_setup_cost.resource_effect: parallel CPU, worker memory and instantaneous IO throughput normally fall; throughput is intentionally not modeled in T
parallel_setup_cost.historical_relation: semantic CPU sign conflicts with the old joint vector; plan scan contains Gather and Gather Merge, so this remains a low-confidence probe prior

parallel_tuple_cost.plan_effect: higher cost discourages tuple transfer through Gather and parallel plans
parallel_tuple_cost.resource_effect: parallel CPU, worker memory and instantaneous IO throughput normally fall; throughput is intentionally not modeled in T
parallel_tuple_cost.historical_relation: semantic CPU sign conflicts with the old joint vector; no independent coordinate evidence

canonicalization: UTF-8 JSON of table only, sort_keys=true, separators=(',', ':')
